subject: Pricing: threshold escape clause & blended on-demand tiers
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Jenna Ortiz <jenna.ortiz@bluebay.ai>
Cc: procurement@bluebay.ai
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Pricing proposal — thresholds + on-demand tiers

Jenna,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, I attached a concise pricing sheet and a short SOW draft — high level summary below.

Key points (proposal):
- Minimum monthly commitment: $25,000 (applies to billed usage each calendar month).
- Blended on-demand tiers when commit is exceeded: 1) Spike Window rate = 1.9x the committed unit rate for the first 48 hours of a usage spike, billed separately as a "spike window" line item; 2) Sustained overage rate = 1.25x committed unit rate for sustained on-demand usage beyond the spike window.
- True-up cadence: quarterly true-up with the option to convert overage into next-quarter commit credit at a 0.9x conversion factor (encourages predictable commits).
- Escape clause (customer request): allow a one-time temporary reduction to the minimum in case of a documented, company-wide launch or force major outage for BlueBay. Limit: one event per 12 months, reduction not to exceed 50% of the monthly minimum, requires 14 days prior notice where possible or documented post-event justification.

Open items we asked BlueBay about: whether procurement needs a firm annual cap on aggregate overage dollars, and whether legal insists on force majeure-only language vs a controlled operational "escape" for recognized business events.

Next steps:
1) Confirm procurement's preference on annual overage cap and whether the escape clause language above is acceptable.
2) If yes, we'll share a redline of the SOW + a short contract rider with explicit tier math and invoice examples.

Attaching: redwood-pricing-sheet-v2.pdf, draft-sow-bluebay.docx

Best,

Soojin

Soojin,

Thanks — appreciate the clarity. A couple quick clarifications from procurement:
- They want to understand how the spike window triggers are detected (metric thresholds or human flag). Can you add a definition and a sample invoice showing a spike window charge vs sustained overage?
- The escape clause language sounds promising, but legal will likely push back on anything that looks like an open-ended adjustment. They asked if we can limit the escape clause to two discrete event types: (a) major product launches that are communicated in advance, or (b) documented cloud-region outages caused by a third-party provider.
- Also, procurement asked if there's a simple annual cap option we can provide (e.g., cap overage to 40% of annual committed dollars) in exchange for a slightly lower committed minimum.

Can you loop in pricing/legal from your side? If we can get a concise redline and an example invoice, procurement can move quickly.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pricing proposal — thresholds + on-demand tiers

Soojin / Marissa,

Thanks for the context. My take and suggested contract language below.

Summary recommendations:
- Define "Spike Window" as: an increase in 1-minute QPS of greater than 3x the 30-day rolling average sustained for at least 10 minutes, or a human-declared business event (with email notice). The system will flag candidate spikes and finance will review invoice artifacts if contested.
- Limit the Escape Clause to: (1) a documented product launch (evidence required — press release or customer notice) and (2) a third-party provider outage impacting >20% of BlueBay traffic for >= 4 hours. One-time use per 12-month period, reduction up to 50% of monthly minimum.
- Annual overage cap option (optional rider): cap aggregate overage charges to 40% of annual committed dollars in exchange for reducing minimum by 15%. If cap is reached, on-demand pricing above the cap converts to a negotiated enterprise spot rate for the remainder of the year.
- Keep quarterly true-up, but change conversion factor to 0.85x for conservative economics.

Draft wording (short):
"Spike Window" means the initial 48-hour period after a detected usage spike (per the detection algorithm above) during which usage above the committed rate shall be billed at the Spike Window Rate. "Escape Event" means a product launch or third-party outage meeting thresholds above; customer may invoke Escape Event relief one time per 12-month period with supporting documentation.

Finance thumbs-up items: 1) 1.9x spike rate + 1.25x sustained provides reasonable margin; 2) 0.85x conversion keeps expected revenue higher than 0.9x conversion; 3) annual cap at 40% is acceptable if we attach a commercial rider that triggers a renegotiation if cap is exceeded.

Attaching a proposed redline and an example invoice template (I put sample math for a $25k minimum and a 2-week launch spike).

-Karthik
VP, Pricing & Commercial Operations
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Attached are: (1) a redlined SOW + rider that includes the Spike Window detection definition and escape clause limits, (2) an invoice example showing a sample 12-day launch spike and how the spike window vs sustained overage would bill, and (3) a short DocuSign invite we can send if BlueBay wants to accept the optional capped-overage rider.

Highlights for procurement/legal:

- Escape Event limited to the two event types with one-time annual use and max 50% reduction to monthly minimum.
- Optional annual overage cap rider: 40% cap in exchange for a 15% reduction to monthly minimum; if cap is hit we convert further overages to enterprise spot rate for remainder of term and trigger renegotiation.

If this looks good, I'll send a DocuSign packet containing: SOW (redline), the optional rider (if they want the cap), and a short signature page. If procurement wants an in-person walkthrough on the invoice examples, I can set 30 minutes next week.
